findings.claim: GE Vernova's gas turbine backlog stretches into 2029 (sold out through 2028, less than 10% remaining capacity in 2029), while Bloom ships fuel cell systems within months — Bloom's time-to-power gap vs. gas turbines widened as GEV's Q2 2026 data center orders exceeded $5B YTD (more than double all of 2025) on a $176B total backlog.
findings.source: The Motley Fool, "GE Vernova vs. Bloom Energy: Which AI-Power Bet Has More Upside Ahead?" (2026-08-28)

findings.claim: Bloom Energy Q2 2026 revenue surged 166% YoY to $1.07B (first billion-dollar quarter), gross margin rose to 33.4% (+668bps YoY), operating income was $182.2M (vs. -$3.5M loss in Q2 2025), and FY2026 revenue guidance was raised to $3.9-4.2B (~100% YoY growth); order backlog reached $20B, described by the company as growing faster than revenue due to supply constraints, with all major U.S. hyperscalers plus over a dozen neoclouds/AI labs/colocation operators having validated Bloom's power solutions.
findings.source: BigGo Finance, "[BE Q2 2026 Earnings Call] Bloom Energy Reports First Billion-Dollar Quarter, Raises FY2026 Revenue Guidance" (2026-07-28)

findings.claim: Bloom's competitors span gas turbine/large power OEMs (GE Vernova, Siemens Energy, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries), reciprocating engine makers (Caterpillar, Cummins), and direct fuel-cell peers (FuelCell Energy with MCFC tech for large-scale carbon capture/long-duration storage, Plug Power dominant in mobility/forklift/trucking hydrogen rather than stationary baseload); market commentary characterizes Bloom's SOFC as best-positioned for stationary baseload power specifically, implying differentiated rather than head-to-head share loss against these peers as of mid-2026.
findings.source: Hudson Labs, "Bloom Energy Competitors: BE Top Peers 2026"; corroborated by PitchBook Bloom Energy company profile

findings.claim: On 2026-04-13, Bloom Energy and Oracle announced an expanded strategic partnership under which Oracle plans to procure up to 2.8 GW of Bloom's fuel cell systems (up from 1.2 GW already contracted and being deployed) to power Oracle's U.S. AI and cloud data centers — a deepening of Oracle's commitment to Bloom as sole fuel-cell supplier for this program, with no disclosed move by Oracle toward in-house fuel cell development or a second fuel-cell vendor.
findings.source: Bloom Energy investor press release, "Bloom Energy and Oracle Expand Strategic Partnership to Deploy up to 2.8 GW" (investor.bloomenergy.com, 2026-04-13)

findings.claim: Brookfield's $5B partnership (up to $5B to fund deployment of Bloom's SOFC technology at AI data centers worldwide) structures Brookfield as capital/asset owner-operator while Bloom remains the sole technology/equipment supplier — search results found no evidence of Brookfield, Oracle, AEP, Nebius, Equinix, or SK ecoplant adding a second fuel-cell source or insourcing SOFC manufacturing as of the search date.
findings.source: Data Center Dynamics, "Bloom Energy signs $5bn partnership with Brookfield to deploy fuel cell tech at AI data centers"

findings.claim: Bloom Energy's own supply chain (not customer-side second-sourcing) shows dependency risk: a Hunterbrook Media short-seller report (2026-07-08, "Bloom's Big Lie") alleged Bloom is dependent on a Chinese supplier (Hunan Oriental Scandium) for scandium oxide feedstock and that 5GW production targets would require ~220 tons of scandium annually against a projected global supply of ~240 tons; Bloom publicly rebutted the claims as "false and misleading," stating it is not China-dependent for scandium oxide and has visibility to support 25GW/year fuel cell production. This is a Bloom-side input-supplier concentration issue, not evidence of a customer second-sourcing Bloom itself.
findings.source: TradingView News, "Bloom Energy rebuts short-seller report, defends scandium supply and financials" (2026-07-09)

A separate disclosure cited three customers accounting for roughly 43%, 13%, and 12% of total sales.

findings.claim: For the three months ended 2026-03-31, U.S. revenue was 91% of Bloom Energy's total revenue, indicating high geographic concentration alongside customer concentration (exposure to U.S. energy policy, natural gas prices, and regulatory change).
findings.source: Bloom Energy Corp Form 10-Q, SEC EDGAR (filed for period ended 2026-03-31)

findings.claim: S&P Global Ratings downgraded Oracle's credit rating to BBB- (one notch above junk) in July 2026, citing negative free cash flow of -$23.7B for fiscal year ended May 2026, debt of $129.5B (~4.3x EBITDA, above the 4x threshold signaling financial strain), and roughly $260B of committed data-center leases; S&P analyst Andrew Chang said a further downgrade is possible if leverage stays above 4.5x, and Moody's also holds a negative outlook on Oracle. Oracle is one of Bloom Energy's largest disclosed customers (2.8GW fuel-cell commitment).
findings.source: Yahoo Finance / Reuters syndication, "Oracle stock shrugs off S&P downgrade to 'BBB-'" and "Oracle's Credit Risk Nears an 18-Year High" (2026-07)

findings.claim: As of August 2026, Bloom Energy faces fresh AI-data-center power competition from natural gas turbines (Chevron and Microsoft rolling out gas turbine projects for data center power) and from a U.S. Department of Energy program financing next-generation nuclear reactors (SMRs) targeting the same AI data center demand; however, commentary assessed that SMRs face lengthy regulatory hurdles and public-acceptance issues and that none will be commercially deployed at scale within the next 5-7 years, leaving that as Bloom's entrenchment window, with micro-nuclear (~5-50MW) proposals aimed at the 2030s.
findings.source: Simply Wall St News, "Bloom Energy (BE) Faces New AI Power Competition From Chevron Microsoft And Nuclear" (2026-08)

findings.claim: Starting in 2026, Bloom Energy's Energy Servers qualify for a 30% investment tax credit under IRA Section 48E, improving customer economics relative to substitute on-site generation technologies (gas turbines, reciprocating engines).
findings.source: Simply Wall St News, "Bloom Energy (BE) Faces New AI Power Competition From Chevron Microsoft And Nuclear" (2026-08)
